solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: 5 in malice hail corrupt political 29

indicators.note: corrupted letters are spoiled and rearranged

explanation.surface: Something numbered five, hailed with malice, stands in a line about a corrupt political thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: The '5' is not a cross-reference to 5 Down but the Roman numeral V, which joins the anagram. 29 is PHILOSOPHER, so the definition reads 'political philosopher'.
explanation.definitionFit: Niccolò Machiavelli, author of The Prince, is the classic political philosopher.

clue.text: Optimism at Chevening masks conflict

indicators.note: the phrase covers the answer, which sits concealed inside it

explanation.surface: Cheerful talk at a diplomatic residence papers over a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: Chevening is the British Foreign Secretary's official country house, which makes the diplomatic scene plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, as a noun: two things that clash are said to be in conflict.

clue.text: Black stray in Galilean location and city

indicators.note: 'in' places one thing inside another

parts.note: the Galilee village of the wedding feast in John's Gospel
to wander from the right path

explanation.surface: A dark stray animal wanders in a biblical spot and then a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black stray' reads as a dog or cat, but the two words split into separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Australian capital is one city among many.

clue.text: Laity all over the place in Catholic country

indicators.note: the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Lay churchgoers are scattered across a Catholic nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The laity are the non-clergy members of a church, which ties the fodder neatly to the Catholic setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: home of the Vatican, it is a largely Catholic nation.

clue.text: Those watching six large water vessels

explanation.surface: An audience keeps an eye on half a dozen big jugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water vessels' suggests boats, but these are jugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a television audience is made up of people who watch.

clue.text: Crime racket here and there in two American cities

indicators.note: take letters from scattered spots: every other one
'in' places one thing inside another, so the racket's letters sit between the two cities

explanation.surface: A criminal racket operates in two US cities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racket' in the surface is organised crime, which sits well beside the definition, but here it only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: theft is one particular crime, and this is its legal name.

clue.text: Hindrance in Spain interrupting La Diablada?

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something

parts.note: La Diablada is a dance of devils, so an imp dance

explanation.surface: Something gets in the way of a Spanish-speaking folk festival.
explanation.walkthrough: La Diablada is an Andean festival dance of masked devils; the question mark flags that 'imp dance' is a playful description of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: anything that impedes is a hindrance, and in electronics the word names resistance to current.

clue.text: Fruit — predatory bird wanting kilo

parts.note: K is kilo in the phonetic alphabet; it is removed

explanation.surface: A hawk, minus a kilo, is described as fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting' in the surface could be hungry, fitting a predator, but it means without.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the red berry of the hawthorn is one kind of fruit.

clue.text: Secret plan Häagen-Dazs suggests?

definitions.meaning: a straight definition of a concealed scheme
the surface points to an ice-cream brand; the setter means the letters of the name, which conceal a six-letter word for a plan

explanation.surface: An ice-cream brand hints at a secret scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the brand as a crossword clue would: AGENDA is literally hidden inside HäAGEN-DAzs, so the name contains a hidden agenda.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an ulterior motive kept out of sight is a concealed programme, a secret plan.

clue.text: Hot stuff, did you see me hugging sailor?

indicators.note: a hug wraps arms around someone

parts.note: the question 'Was I?', as in was I seen

explanation.surface: Someone asks if they were spotted cuddling a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot stuff' suggests something sexy, which the hugging surface plays on, but it is spicy food.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the fiery green Japanese paste is one kind of hot stuff.

clue.text: Motorsport icon Boleyn and Cleves recalled?

indicators.note: called back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Anne Boleyn and Anne of Cleves, two of Henry VIII's wives

explanation.surface: A racing legend brings to mind two of Henry VIII's queens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' seems to mean remembered, as of history, but it asks for the letters to come back the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Ayrton, the Brazilian triple Formula One champion, is a motorsport icon.

clue.text: Dramatist in Eire is with DUP surprisingly

indicators.note: the letters come out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A playwright in Ireland is unexpectedly in league with the DUP.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland, so a dramatist in Eire siding with it would be surprising.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: one of the three great Athenian tragedians is a dramatist.

clue.text: Celt with an eye out for C2H2

indicators.note: the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A Celt keeps a lookout for a chemical formula.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With an eye out for' reads as watching for something; 'out' is really the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemical formula: two carbons and two hydrogens make the welding gas.

clue.text: Nerd one Royal Society girl embraces

indicators.note: an embrace holds someone within the arms, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: the royal 'we', a monarch's word for oneself

explanation.surface: A geek is hugged by a debutante from the Royal Society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Royal Society' looks like the scientific academy, which suits a nerd, but the phrase must be split across two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, American slang for a socially awkward swot.

clue.text: Say red and white containers?

parts.note: the surface suggests colours, as of a flag or a football strip; the setter means vessels for red and white wine, 'say' marking an example

explanation.surface: A question about vessels painted in red and white.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark warns that the definition is oblique: the containers hold wine rather than being coloured.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: glass flasks used to serve house wines of either colour.

clue.text: Identify suspect advice in digital feature

parts.note: slang: to point the finger at a culprit

explanation.surface: Advice on picking out a suspect via some digital technology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital' is not about computers: digits are fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: Pun on 'digital': the end of a digit is a feature of it.

clue.text: New Englander's tooth extraction technique?

definitions.meaning: short for Yankee, a word first used of people from the north-eastern US states

explanation.surface: A dentist from Massachusetts has a signature way of pulling teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe s reads as 'is', joining the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: slang for an American, originally a northeasterner, and a sharp tug.

clue.text: Stock pirate feature (archetype possibly not right)

indicators.note: the letters might be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A stereotypical pirate's trademark is described as an archetype, maybe not quite right.
explanation.walkthrough: The parenthesis reads as a comment on the definition, but it is the whole of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the cliché one-eyed buccaneer wears one over the missing eye.

clue.text: Cockney perhaps briefly sustained by kebab

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: long means sustained, lasting a long time
a doner is a kebab of meat sliced from a rotating spit

explanation.surface: An East Ender briefly kept going by a late-night kebab.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney is a working-class Londoner from the East End, so the definition is an example, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Every Cockney is by tradition born within the sound of Bow Bells in London, making one a Londoner.

clue.text: U-boat carrying any number turned up

indicators.note: a vessel carrying cargo holds it inside

parts.note: N is the algebraic symbol for any number

explanation.surface: A German submarine with an unknown number aboard surfaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' looks like a reversal instruction, but it is the definition: a snub nose is turned up at the tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective sense: a short nose tilted at the end is described this way.

clue.text: Rice dish one with no meat served up

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent upwards, so the letters run backwards

explanation.surface: A rice dish is dished up by someone who adds no meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Served up' fits the food surface; in a down clue it means read from the bottom upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a spiced South Asian dish is one based on rice.

clue.text: Earl with most suitable temper receiving love now and then

parts.note: as in 'the very thing', exactly right

explanation.surface: An aristocrat with the ideal temperament mellows, receiving love from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Temper' reads as a noun, a mood, but it is the verb meaning to tone down.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: both phrases mean occasionally.

clue.text: Composer leaving area green for painter

indicators.note: the composer is leaving, that is going away from, the area, so A departs

explanation.surface: A composer quits the environmental patch to make way for an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Area green' reads as a village green, but the two words have separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Cretan-born master of Renaissance Toledo is a painter.

clue.text: See 7
Ailment endless with a river animal

indicators.note: endless means without its final letter

parts.note: a cough is a minor ailment
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: An animal with a persistent illness by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' looks like it describes a never-ending ailment, but it docks the last letter of COUGH.
explanation.definitionFit: The cougar, also called puma or mountain lion, is a large wild cat of the Americas.

clue.text: Maxim the Obscure Financier

definitions.meaning: a faceless Swiss banker, in a famous British political jibe

explanation.surface: Reads like the title of a novel or film about a mysterious moneyman.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'gnomes of Zurich' was Harold Wilson's era phrase for secretive Swiss bankers.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a rare word for an aphorism, and a disparaging term for a shadowy banker.

clue.text: Ginger fed with fish almost rallied

indicators.note: something fed with food takes it inside, so the colour takes the fish in
the last letter is dropped

parts.note: GROUPER, a sea fish, without its last letter

explanation.surface: A ginger cat, fed some fish, nearly recovered its spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ginger' looks like the spice or a cat, but it is a hair colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: troops that gather again after a setback have rallied.

clue.text: Architectural feature in Kosovo lovely

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the phrase

explanation.surface: Praise for a building detail in a Balkan country.
explanation.walkthrough: This is an obscure term, so the hidden word is the way in; crossers help confirm it.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a rounded convex moulding in classical building.

clue.text: Horse chasing man discussed bad experience

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so the horse comes after
discussed means spoken about, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: A horse running after a chess piece in a game that has gone badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is a chess piece, the knight; said aloud it gives NIGHT, and MARE follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightmare is a frightening dream, and by extension any very unpleasant experience.

clue.text: See 20
Simple tune not bad sans introduction

indicators.note: sans is French for without, so the word loses its introduction, the opening letter

explanation.surface: A plain melody that is passable apart from its opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not bad' is a single idea, passable, not a negation to act on.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a song or melody, as in Bach's Air on the G String.

clue.text: Polish hero damaged absorbing pressure one thinks

definitions.note: the definition is a clause, 'one [who] thinks', standing for the noun

indicators.note: the letters are broken and remade

explanation.surface: A wounded Polish hero, under strain, ponders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' tempts as a nationality, but it is plain anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive: a professional thinker, one whose trade is thought.
